newsitem.title: GERMANY: Austria to seek EU jobs, tax coordination - Klima.
newsitem.headline: Austria to seek EU jobs, tax coordination - Klima.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima said he would press the European Union (EU) to coordinate members' jobs initiatives, but did not want Brussels to subsidize programs for members hit with high unemployment.

"We need a jobs pact and Austria will vehemently demand it at the EU government conference," said Klima, who replaced Franz Vranitzky as head of Austria's Social Democrat coalition 10 days ago, in an interview with the weekly Der Spiegel.

"We want no new money for any old senseless project in any old country," he said. The EU needs "a (jobs) goal and then collective monitoring of the effectiveness of the chosen measures. The prescriptions can be different from country to country."
Klima also said EU labour ministers have to fight harder to preserve jobs initiatives despite budget cuts to meet European monetary union requirements.

"Just as finance ministers work to keep budget discipline, so must labour and technology ministers work to look after the employment level, and they should be embarrassed if they fail to reduce the number of jobless," Klima said.
"What I really mean to say is: Break the power of the finance ministers," said Klima, who was Austria's finance minister until taking his current post.
Austria should fight unemployment by building up an information insfrastructure that would support new types of high-tech jobs, Klima said.

He also called for the EU to harmonise members' tax systems to reduce competition between EU nations in attracting jobs and investment. "Here the EU plays a deciding role," he said. "We need a harmonisation of tax systems, but not a leveling."

Klima also ruled out a coalition or even backroom dealings with right-wing Freedom Pary leader Joerg Haider. "Social Democracy under my leadership will under no circumstances enter a coalition with Haider," he said.
